title: Dr. Geoff Lindsey: Modern RP (Received Pronunciation) & Acoustic Phonetics
author: Dr. Geoff Lindsey (PhD, Linguistics, University College London)

modern_rp_vowel_shifts.description: Modern British speakers pronounce TRAP as a fully open front vowel [a], not the tense, raised [æ] of 1950s BBC or General American.
Crucial distinction for non-native speakers: /ʊ/ in 'put', 'book' is rounded and near-back; /ʌ/ in 'cut', 'strut' is open-mid central [ɐ].
The FLEECE vowel is not a static monophthong; it is phonetically a closing diphthong starting near [ɪ] and ending in high glide [j].
